sentences.text: The holotype skull of Guidraco measures 38 cm in length and features distinctive teeth, including a long, narrow first upper tooth followed by three enormous, robust, pointed, and slightly recurved teeth.

Guidraco was described and named by Wang Xiaolin, Alexander W.A. Kellner, Jiang Shunxing, and Cheng Xin in 2012 based on the holotype specimen IVPP V17083, which was collected from the Jiufotang Formation near Sihedang, Liaoning Province.

According to many recent studies, Guidraco belongs to the subfamily Anhanguerinae within the family Anhangueridae. Later analyses in 2019 reassigned Guidraco to the subfamily Anhanguerinae, identifying it as a sister taxon to the genera Caulkicephalus and Ludodactylus.
This animal lived during the Aptian stage, between 121.4 and 113.2 million years ago.
In 2014, Brian Andres and colleagues recovered an alternate phylogenetic position for Guidraco within the family Boreopteridae.
